B1-g0-C1.title: Bounded leave-one-out z-score fusion (LOO-Z) for per-image MVFA scoring
B1-g0-C1.summary: Standardise MVFA's zero-shot and few-shot maps with leave-one-out statistics of the K support normals, clip them to a bounded range, fuse with inverse-variance weights and pool the top 2% pixels, so every image is scored on its own.
B1-g0-C1.research_idea: Independent variable: the fusion rule (transductive test-set min-max + 0.5 sum vs. LOO-Z). LOO-Z computes, for each branch b in {zero, few} and level l, the mean and standard deviation of patch scores of the K support normals, where the few-shot score of support i is computed against a memory bank built from the other K-1 supports (leave-one-out) and the zero-shot score uses the text anchors as usual. Each test patch score is converted to z = (s - mu_bl)/sigma_bl, clipped to [-3, 6] (bounded drift), summed over levels, and the two branches are combined with weights w_b proportional to 1/Var(LOO image scores of branch b). The image score is the mean of the top 2% fused pixels. Dependent variables: image-/pixel-level AUROC, sensitivity/specificity/F1 at the threshold tau = 95th percentile of support LOO image scores, ECE of the logistic-mapped score, and the stability of AUROC under test-set subsampling and prevalence shift.
B1-g0-C1.hypothesis: On held-out BMAD modalities with K >= 4, LOO-Z fusion achieves image- and pixel-level AUROC within 1 point of MVFA's transductive fusion while its AUROC varies at least 3x less across random 50% test subsamples and 10%/50% prevalence resamples, and its support-derived threshold yields realised specificity within 5 points of the nominal 95%.
B1-g0-C1.rationale: The chain moves from MVFA's transductive fusion (test-set min-max, fixed 0.5) to methods that score each image against references only (MadCLIP) and that bound how far a per-image adjustment can move (ReCAP). The missing step for MVFA is to replace test-set statistics with reference statistics from the K normal supports and to bound each branch's contribution so neither dominates, which yields a deployable per-image score and a threshold that can be set before seeing target labels.
B1-g0-C1.method: 1) test_few.py: refactor scoring into score_image(x, supports) that never touches other test images. 2) Support statistics (new function support_stats in utils.py): for each support normal i, build memory banks from the other K-1 supports at each level l (det and seg tokens as in MVFA), compute few-shot patch scores 1 - max cos; compute zero-shot patch scores softmax(100 * f_l @ T)[abnormal]; store mu_bl, sigma_bl (sigma floored at 1e-3) and the LOO image scores. For K=2 the LOO bank contains a single image; statistics are pooled over all 289 patches x 4 levels so they remain defined. 3) For a test image: z_bl = clip((s_bl - mu_bl)/sigma_bl, -3, 6); Z_b = sum_l z_bl upsampled to 240x240; F = w_zero Z_zero + w_few Z_few with w_b = (1/v_b)/(1/v_zero + 1/v_few), v_b the variance of branch b's LOO image scores. 4) Image score = mean of top 2% of F (about 1,150 of 57,600 pixels; ablations: max, mean, top 1%, top 5%). 5) Threshold tau = 95th percentile of support LOO image scores; probability via Platt mapping fitted on support LOO scores with pseudo-negatives only is not identifiable, so ECE is computed after mapping p = sigmoid((score - tau)/s) with s = support score IQR. 6) No training changes; reuse MVFA checkpoints trained under the shared protocol.
B1-g0-C1.experiment: Protocol: BMAD, leave-one-modality-out (RESC and OCT17 held out together), checkpoints of the underlying MVFA model selected on a validation split of the source modalities (never the target test set); MVFA baseline re-run under the same rule; K in {2,4,8,16}; 3 seeds x 3 support draws (new seed files generated from BMAD valid/ with a fixed RNG); mean and standard deviation reported. Baselines: MVFA transductive fusion (released code); MVFA with per-image fusion but no normalisation (raw sum); LOO-Z without clipping; LOO-Z with equal weights. Ablations: aggregation operator; K. Metrics: image AUROC, pixel AUROC, PRO; sensitivity, specificity, F1 at tau; ECE; AUROC standard deviation over 20 random 50% test subsamples and under prevalence resampling to 10% and 50% abnormal. Falsification: if LOO-Z loses more than 2 AUROC points on average, or its AUROC is not more stable than the transductive fusion, the hypothesis is rejected.
provenance: MadCLIP: Few-shot Medical Anomaly Detection with CLIP
Beyond Static Anchors: Bounded Prototype Conditioning for Language-Free Medical Anomaly Detection

B1-g0-C2.title: Empirical p-value fusion across levels and branches (Fisher-MVFA)
B1-g0-C2.summary: Turn each level/branch patch score into an empirical p-value against support-normal LOO scores and combine them with Fisher's method, giving a per-image, distribution-free anomaly statistic and a principled threshold.
B1-g0-C2.research_idea: Independent variable: combination rule (raw sum + test-set min-max vs. empirical p-value fusion). For each branch b and level l, the null distribution is the set of LOO patch scores of the K support normals. A test patch score s gets p_bl = (1 + #{null >= s}) / (1 + N_null). The fused pixel statistic is X = -2 * sum_{b,l} log p_bl (Fisher), and the image statistic is the mean of the top 2% pixels of X. Because X is built from tail probabilities, a threshold can be read from the support LOO image statistics. Dependent variables: AUROC (image, pixel), PRO, thresholded sensitivity/specificity/F1, ECE, and per-level contribution analysis.
B1-g0-C2.hypothesis: On held-out BMAD modalities, Fisher p-value fusion matches MVFA's transductive fusion within 1 AUROC point for K >= 4, and its support-derived threshold achieves a realised false-positive rate within 5 points of nominal, whereas a raw-sum per-image fusion without test-set normalisation loses at least 3 AUROC points.
B1-g0-C2.rationale: MVFA and MLCA add the four levels' raw maps and then min-max them over the test set; levels have different score scales, so the sum is dominated by whichever level has the largest spread. Converting every level and branch score into an empirical tail probability against the support normals puts all evidence on a common, calibrated scale and makes the combination inductive.
B1-g0-C2.method: 1) utils.py: add null_scores(supports) returning, per branch and level, the sorted 1-D array of LOO patch scores (K x 289 values) and empirical_p(s, null) via np.searchsorted. 2) test_few.py: for each test image compute p_bl for all 289 patches at each of 4 levels and 2 branches, X_patch = -2 sum log p (16 x 16-bit floats per patch), bilinearly upsample X to 240x240; image score = mean of top 2%. 3) Ties and extreme scores: p is floored at 1/(1+N_null), so X is bounded. 4) Threshold: 95th percentile of the support LOO image statistics. 5) Variant: weighted Fisher with level weights estimated from the separability of LOO normals vs. the other branch (no target labels). 6) No retraining.
B1-g0-C2.experiment: Protocol: BMAD, leave-one-modality-out (RESC and OCT17 held out together), checkpoints of the underlying MVFA model selected on a validation split of the source modalities (never the target test set); MVFA baseline re-run under the same rule; K in {2,4,8,16}; 3 seeds x 3 support draws (new seed files generated from BMAD valid/ with a fixed RNG); mean and standard deviation reported. Baselines: transductive MVFA fusion; per-image raw sum; LOO-Z (z-score fusion) as a parametric alternative. Ablations: Fisher vs. Stouffer vs. min-p combination; per-level vs. all-level null pools; aggregation operator. Metrics as in the problem. Falsification: AUROC loss above 2 points or realised FPR deviating by more than 10 points from nominal.
provenance: Fine-Tuning CLIP Models with Convolutional Features for Medical Anomaly Detection

B1-g0-C3.title: Support-synthesised Platt calibration for inductive MVFA fusion
B1-g0-C3.summary: Create synthetic anomalies on the K support normals, fit a two-feature logistic calibrator (zero-shot and few-shot image scores) on support normals versus their synthetic versions, and use it to score each test image without test-set statistics.
B1-g0-C3.research_idea: Independent variables: fusion rule (transductive 0.5 sum vs. learned logistic fusion) and synthetic anomaly family (CutPaste-style patches from other supports, Perlin-noise intensity perturbations, local Gaussian blur/contrast changes). For each support normal, generate M = 8 synthetic abnormal versions with known masks; compute per-image features [top-2% zero-shot score, top-2% few-shot LOO score]; fit logistic regression (Platt) on 8K positives vs. K negatives with class re-weighting. Test images get p = sigma(w^T f + b). Dependent variables: AUROC, ECE, sensitivity at p = 0.5 and at the 95% support specificity point, and how well synthetic-based calibration transfers per modality.
B1-g0-C3.hypothesis: Logistic fusion fitted on support normals and their synthetic anomalies reduces expected calibration error by at least 30% relative to MVFA's min-max scores mapped to [0,1], with image AUROC within 1 point, on held-out BMAD modalities for K >= 4.
B1-g0-C3.rationale: A per-image score needs not only a normal reference (support normals) but also an estimate of what abnormal scores look like at the target site to set a meaningful threshold and to calibrate probabilities. Fed-LoRA shows synthetic abnormal exemplars tailored to a site are useful for MVFA; cheap synthetic anomalies created on the K support normals can provide the abnormal side of a calibration set without any target labels.
B1-g0-C3.method: 1) New file synth.py: cutpaste(x, donor), perlin_intensity(x, scale in {4,8}, alpha in [0.1,0.4]), local_blur(x, sigma in [2,5]); each returns image and mask; anomaly area 1-10% of the image, placed inside the foreground (Otsu mask). 2) In test_few.py before scoring: build the memory bank from supports; for each support i compute LOO few-shot score (bank without i) and zero-shot score for the original and its synthetic versions. 3) Features f = [top2%(zero map), top2%(few map)], standardised with support-normal statistics. 4) sklearn LogisticRegression(C=1.0, class_weight='balanced'). 5) Test: p(x) = model.predict_proba(f(x)); pixel maps fused with the same weights. 6) No retraining of adapters.
B1-g0-C3.experiment: Protocol: BMAD, leave-one-modality-out (RESC and OCT17 held out together), checkpoints of the underlying MVFA model selected on a validation split of the source modalities (never the target test set); MVFA baseline re-run under the same rule; K in {2,4,8,16}; 3 seeds x 3 support draws (new seed files generated from BMAD valid/ with a fixed RNG); mean and standard deviation reported. Baselines: transductive MVFA; LOO-Z fusion; logistic fusion fitted on source-modality validation data instead of synthetic target data. Ablations: synthetic family; M; features (add max and mean). Metrics: ECE (15 bins), Brier score, AUROC, sensitivity/specificity at p=0.5. Falsification: ECE not reduced by 30% or AUROC loss above 2 points.
provenance: Fed-LoRA: Cross-Domain Generative Knowledge Feedback for Few-Shot Medical Anomaly Detection

B1-g0-C4.title: Shrinkage-Gaussian Mahalanobis scoring of support normals for inductive few-shot fusion
B1-g0-C4.summary: Replace the few-shot branch's max-cosine memory search with per-level Mahalanobis distances under a Ledoit-Wolf Gaussian fitted to support patch features, standardise by its chi-square reference, and fuse per image with the zero-shot branch.
B1-g0-C4.research_idea: Independent variable: few-shot scoring (memory-bank 1 - max cosine with test-set min-max vs. per-level Gaussian Mahalanobis with analytic standardisation). For each level l, fit mu_l and Sigma_l (Ledoit-Wolf shrinkage, features projected to the top-d PCA components of support patches, d = min(64, K*289-1)) on all support normal patches. Patch score m = (f - mu)^T Sigma^-1 (f - mu), standardised as (m - d)/sqrt(2d). The zero-shot branch is standardised with support LOO statistics as in LOO-Z, and the image score is the top-2% mean of the fused map. Dependent variables: AUROC, PRO, thresholded metrics, stability under subsampling, memory and time per image.
B1-g0-C4.hypothesis: Per-level shrinkage-Gaussian scoring yields few-shot pixel AUROC within 1 point of MVFA's memory-bank branch and, combined inductively, an image-level threshold whose realised specificity is within 5 points of nominal, while reducing few-shot branch memory by more than 90% for K = 16.
B1-g0-C4.rationale: Nearest-neighbour distances to a handful of support patches are noisy and have no natural scale, which is why MVFA must normalise them with test-set extremes. A per-level Gaussian model of support normal features (as compact as Spatial-FAD's prototypes) yields Mahalanobis distances whose distribution under normality is approximately known, so scores become comparable across images and modalities without test-set statistics.
B1-g0-C4.method: 1) utils.py: fit_gaussian(level_feats): PCA (sklearn) to d dims, LedoitWolf().fit; store mu, precision. 2) test_few.py: replace anomaly_map_few_shot = min(1-cos) with mahalanobis per patch at each level; standardise (m - d)/sqrt(2d); clip to [-3, 10]. 3) Fusion: F = Z_zero + Z_few (both per-image standardised), top-2% image pooling, threshold from support LOO. 4) Memory: store only mu (d), precision (d x d), PCA basis per level. 5) No retraining.
B1-g0-C4.experiment: Protocol: BMAD, leave-one-modality-out (RESC and OCT17 held out together), checkpoints of the underlying MVFA model selected on a validation split of the source modalities (never the target test set); MVFA baseline re-run under the same rule; K in {2,4,8,16}; 3 seeds x 3 support draws (new seed files generated from BMAD valid/ with a fixed RNG); mean and standard deviation reported. Baselines: MVFA memory bank (transductive); memory bank with LOO-Z normalisation; Gaussian without PCA. Ablations: d; shrinkage vs. empirical covariance; per-level vs. pooled Gaussian. Metrics: AUROC, PRO, thresholded metrics, memory (MB), ms/image. Falsification: pixel AUROC loss above 2 points.
provenance: Bridging Vision Foundation Model Priors with CLIP for Spatial-aware Few-shot Anomaly Detection in Medical Images

B1-g0-C5.title: Region-mass aggregation: scoring images by their strongest coherent anomalous region
B1-g0-C5.summary: Threshold each image's per-image-normalised fused map at a support-derived pixel level, extract connected regions, and score the image by the best region's mean score weighted by log area, replacing the max-pixel rule.
B1-g0-C5.research_idea: Independent variable: image aggregation (max pixel, mean, top-2% mean, region mass). Region mass: given the per-image fused map F (LOO-Z standardised), threshold at t_pix = 99th percentile of support LOO pixel scores, find 8-connected components, and score each component c as mean(F_c) * log(1 + |c|); image score = max over components (0 if none). Dependent variables: image AUROC, false positives per image at the support threshold, sensitivity for small lesions (lesion area below 1% of the image), and robustness to injected single-pixel noise.
B1-g0-C5.hypothesis: Region-mass aggregation reduces false positives at the support-derived threshold by at least 25% relative to max-pixel aggregation on held-out BMAD modalities with masks (BrainMRI, LiverCT, RESC), with image AUROC within 1 point, and its AUROC degrades less than max pooling when 0.1% of pixels are corrupted with random spikes.
B1-g0-C5.rationale: MVFA's image score for masked datasets is the single maximum of the fused map, so one spurious pixel decides the label; PSMP-CLIP's move from pixel thresholds to region prompts suggests that anomalies should be scored as coherent regions. A region-level aggregation that requires spatial support for a high score is robust to isolated outliers and works per image.
B1-g0-C5.method: 1) test_few.py: after computing the per-image fused map F (LOO-Z as base normalisation), compute t_pix from support LOO maps; mask = F > t_pix; scipy.ndimage.label(mask, structure=ones(3,3)); for each label compute mean(F[label]) and area; score = max(mean * log(1+area)). 2) Robustness test: add spikes to 0.1% of pixels of F with value max(F)+1 before aggregation. 3) Small-lesion subset: test abnormal images with mask area < 1%. 4) Datasets without masks (OCT17, ChestXray, HIS): apply the same rule to the fused det/seg map. 5) No retraining.
B1-g0-C5.experiment: Protocol: BMAD, leave-one-modality-out (RESC and OCT17 held out together), checkpoints of the underlying MVFA model selected on a validation split of the source modalities (never the target test set); MVFA baseline re-run under the same rule; K in {2,4,8,16}; 3 seeds x 3 support draws (new seed files generated from BMAD valid/ with a fixed RNG); mean and standard deviation reported. Baselines: max (MVFA), mean, top-k mean (k in {1%, 2%, 5%}), region mass. Metrics: image AUROC, FP per image and sensitivity at the support threshold, small-lesion sensitivity, AUROC under spike corruption. Falsification: no FP reduction or AUROC loss above 2 points.
provenance: AA-CLIP: Enhancing Zero-Shot Anomaly Detection via Anomaly-Aware CLIP
PSMP-CLIP: Patch-Prompt SAM and Multi-Semantic Prompting for CLIP-Based Zero-Shot Anomaly Detection

B1-g0-C6.title: Causal streaming normalisation of MVFA branch scores from confidently normal arrivals
B1-g0-C6.summary: Initialise branch normalisation from the support normals and update robust statistics (median/MAD) online using only incoming images scored below the current threshold, compared against support-only and test-set normalisation.
B1-g0-C6.research_idea: Independent variable: normalisation source (test-set min-max; support-only LOO-Z; streaming update). Streaming: maintain per-branch, per-level median and MAD of patch scores; start from the support LOO values; after scoring each incoming image, if its image score is below the 80th percentile of the current normal score distribution, update the statistics with an exponential moving estimate (rate 0.05). Order effects are tested with 10 random arrival orders. Dependent variables: AUROC over the stream, realised FPR at the running threshold, drift of the threshold, and sensitivity to prevalence of abnormal arrivals.
B1-g0-C6.hypothesis: Causal streaming normalisation achieves image AUROC within 1 point of transductive MVFA fusion and reduces the across-draw standard deviation of AUROC by at least 30% compared with support-only normalisation at K = 2 and K = 4.
B1-g0-C6.rationale: A deployed MVFA sees images one at a time. Between the purely support-based statistics of LOO-Z (few images, high variance) and test-set min-max (non-causal), a causal alternative updates normalisation statistics online from incoming images that the model itself scores as confidently normal. This keeps scoring per-image and causal while reducing the variance of support-only statistics.
B1-g0-C6.method: 1) test_few.py: wrap scoring in a StreamScorer class with state (median, MAD per branch/level, support-initialised) and update(); stream the test set in a random order (seeded). 2) Scores: z = (s - median)/(1.4826*MAD), clipped as in LOO-Z; image score = top-2% mean. 3) Update rule only on images with score below the 80th percentile of current normal scores (confidently normal). 4) Report results per arrival order and averaged. 5) No retraining.
B1-g0-C6.experiment: Protocol: BMAD, leave-one-modality-out (RESC and OCT17 held out together), checkpoints of the underlying MVFA model selected on a validation split of the source modalities (never the target test set); MVFA baseline re-run under the same rule; K in {2,4,8,16}; 3 seeds x 3 support draws (new seed files generated from BMAD valid/ with a fixed RNG); mean and standard deviation reported. Baselines: transductive MVFA; LOO-Z (support-only); streaming without the confidence gate. Ablations: update rate; gate percentile; prevalence (10%, 30%, 50% abnormal streams). Metrics: AUROC, realised FPR, threshold drift, variance across support draws and arrival orders. Falsification: no variance reduction relative to support-only normalisation.
provenance: G-Anomaly: A Pyramid Graph Transformer-Based Vision-Language Model for General Industrial Anomaly Detection

B1-g1-o1.title: Gaussian-standardised few-shot branch with LOO-Z zero-shot fusion and region-mass pooling
B1-g1-o1.summary: Score each image on its own by fusing an analytically standardised Mahalanobis few-shot map with a support-standardised zero-shot map and pooling the result by its strongest coherent region.
B1-g1-o1.hypothesis: On held-out BMAD modalities with K >= 4, fusing a shrinkage-Gaussian few-shot map ((m - d)/sqrt(2d)) with a LOO-z-scored zero-shot map and pooling by region mass matches MVFA's transductive image AUROC within 1 point while reducing false positives at the support-derived threshold by at least 25% relative to max-pixel pooling.
B1-g1-o1.rationale: Parent 1 (region mass) fixes the verified single-pixel max rule (test_few.py:228) but presupposes a per-image normalised map; parent 2 (Mahalanobis) gives the few-shot branch an analytic reference distribution so it needs no test-set min-max (test_few.py:220). The reviews favoured both for specificity but noted that parent 2 changes more than the fusion and parent 1 only the pooling; together they form a complete per-image pipeline: calibrated branch scores, a bounded sum, and region-level image evidence. Spatial-FAD supports compact support summaries; PSMP-CLIP supports region-level evidence over thresholded pixels.
B1-g1-o1.method: 1) utils.py: fit_gaussian per level on support normal patch tokens (PCA to d = min(64, K*289-1), Ledoit-Wolf). 2) test_few.py: few-shot patch score z_few = clip(((f-mu)^T P (f-mu) - d)/sqrt(2d), -3, 10); zero-shot patch score z_zero = clip((s - mu_zero)/sigma_zero, -3, 6) with support statistics (zero-shot scores of supports need no leave-one-out); sum over 4 levels per branch, upsample to 240x240; F = 0.5(Z_zero + Z_few) (both already standardised). 3) Region mass: t_pix = 99th percentile of support pixel F (supports scored with LOO Gaussian refits for the few-shot term); scipy.ndimage.label on F > t_pix (8-connectivity); image score = max over components of mean(F_c) * log(1+|c|). 4) Image threshold tau = 95th percentile of support LOO image scores. 5) No retraining.
B1-g1-o1.experiment: BMAD leave-one-modality-out (RESC and OCT17 held out together); MVFA checkpoints selected on source-modality validation splits and the MVFA baseline re-run the same way; K in {2,4,8,16}; 3 seeds x 3 support draws, mean and std. Baselines: transductive MVFA; LOO-Z + top-2%; region mass on LOO-Z (parent 1); Gaussian + top-2% (parent 2). Metrics: image/pixel AUROC, PRO, FP per image and sensitivity at tau, AUROC under 0.1% spike corruption and test subsampling. Falsification: AUROC loss > 2 points or no FP reduction vs. top-2% pooling.
provenance: Bridging Vision Foundation Model Priors with CLIP for Spatial-aware Few-shot Anomaly Detection in Medical Images
AA-CLIP: Enhancing Zero-Shot Anomaly Detection via Anomaly-Aware CLIP
PSMP-CLIP: Patch-Prompt SAM and Multi-Semantic Prompting for CLIP-Based Zero-Shot Anomaly Detection

B1-g1-o2.title: LOO-Z inductive fusion with region-mass image scoring and a single support-derived operating point
B1-g1-o2.summary: Combine bounded leave-one-out z-score fusion of MVFA's two branches with region-mass image aggregation, and derive both pixel and image thresholds from the K support normals only.
B1-g1-o2.hypothesis: Replacing MVFA's test-set min-max fusion and max-pixel image score with LOO-Z fusion plus region-mass pooling keeps image AUROC within 1 point on held-out BMAD modalities (K >= 4), reduces AUROC variability across 50% test subsamples by at least 3x, and lowers false positives per image at the support-derived threshold by at least 25%.
B1-g1-o2.rationale: The two parents address the two verified defects of MVFA's few-shot scoring: transductive normalisation (test_few.py:220-241) and max-pixel image scores (test_few.py:228). Reviews preferred LOO-Z for directly fixing fusion and region mass for a concrete robustness test; the combination keeps MVFA's branches unchanged, so any change in results is attributable to scoring alone. MadCLIP and ReCAP show per-image scoring with bounded references is viable; PSMP-CLIP shows region evidence is more stable than pixel thresholds.
B1-g1-o2.method: 1) Support statistics: per branch b and level l, mean/std of LOO patch scores of the K support normals (few-shot bank without the scored support); sigma floored at 1e-3; pooled over patches. 2) Test: z_bl = clip((s_bl - mu_bl)/sigma_bl, -3, 6), Z_b = sum_l z_bl, F = w_zero Z_zero + w_few Z_few with inverse-variance weights from support LOO image scores. 3) Pixel threshold t_pix = 99th percentile of support LOO fused pixels; image score = max over 8-connected components of F > t_pix of mean(F_c) * log(1 + |c|), 0 if none. 4) Image threshold = 95th percentile of support LOO image scores. 5) Code: new module scoring.py with fit_support_stats(), fuse(), region_mass(); test_few.py calls them per image.
B1-g1-o2.experiment: BMAD leave-one-modality-out (RESC and OCT17 held out together); MVFA checkpoints selected on source-modality validation splits and the MVFA baseline re-run the same way; K in {2,4,8,16}; 3 seeds x 3 support draws, mean and std. Baselines: transductive MVFA; LOO-Z + max; LOO-Z + top-2%; raw sum + region mass. Ablations: clipping bounds, weight rule, t_pix percentile. Metrics: image/pixel AUROC, PRO, sensitivity/specificity/F1 at the support threshold, FP per image, AUROC std over 20 subsamples and at 10%/50% prevalence. Falsification: AUROC loss > 2 points or no stability gain.
provenance: MadCLIP: Few-shot Medical Anomaly Detection with CLIP
Beyond Static Anchors: Bounded Prototype Conditioning for Language-Free Medical Anomaly Detection
AA-CLIP: Enhancing Zero-Shot Anomaly Detection via Anomaly-Aware CLIP

B1-g1-o3.title: Intra-image robust normalisation: each image as its own normal reference for per-image MVFA scoring
B1-g1-o3.summary: Normalise every patch score of an image by the robust statistics (median and MAD) of that same image's patch scores, exploiting that most patches of any image are normal, and combine with a support-derived threshold.
B1-g1-o3.hypothesis: Intra-image median/MAD normalisation of each branch's patch scores, fused per image, gives image AUROC within 1 point of MVFA's transductive fusion and reduces AUROC sensitivity to support draws (std across draws) by at least 30% compared with support-only LOO-Z at K = 2 and K = 4.
B1-g1-o3.rationale: The parent calibrates against the support normals, whose statistics are noisy at small K. By analogy with intrinsic-normal-prototype methods (an anomalous image still contains mostly normal tissue), each image provides its own large normal reference: its 289 patches per level. Robust statistics (median, MAD) are insensitive to the minority of anomalous patches, so standardising by them yields a per-image score that needs no test-set statistics and depends little on which supports were drawn. The supports are then used only for the operating threshold.
B1-g1-o3.method: 1) For each test image, branch b and level l: z_blj = (s_blj - median_j s_blj)/(1.4826 MAD_j s_blj + 1e-3). 2) Fused map F = sum over b, l of clip(z, -3, 10); image score = top-2% mean. 3) Threshold: 95th percentile of the same statistic on the support normals (LOO for the few-shot branch). 4) Diffuse anomalies covering more than 50% of an image violate the assumption: add the support-standardised global mean score as a second feature (max of the two after standardisation) as a safeguard. 5) Code: scoring.py intra_image_norm(); test_few.py; no retraining.
B1-g1-o3.experiment: BMAD leave-one-modality-out (RESC and OCT17 held out together); MVFA checkpoints selected on source-modality validation splits and the MVFA baseline re-run the same way; K in {2,4,8,16}; 3 seeds x 3 support draws, mean and std. Baselines: transductive MVFA; LOO-Z; augmentation-conformal calibration. Ablations: with/without the global safeguard; MAD vs IQR. Metrics: image/pixel AUROC, std of AUROC across support draws, realised FPR at the support threshold, performance on images with large lesions (mask area > 30%). Falsification: AUROC loss > 2 points or no reduction in draw sensitivity.
provenance: MadCLIP: Few-shot Medical Anomaly Detection with CLIP
Beyond Static Anchors: Bounded Prototype Conditioning for Language-Free Medical Anomaly Detection

B1-g1-o4.title: Episode-trained fusion calibrator: learning how to fuse MVFA's branches from simulated few-shot episodes on source modalities
B1-g1-o4.summary: Learn, on simulated K-shot episodes drawn from the source modalities' validation splits, a small calibrator that maps support statistics and per-image branch scores to an anomaly probability, then apply it unchanged to the unseen target modality.
B1-g1-o4.hypothesis: A logistic calibrator trained on simulated few-shot episodes from the five source modalities, taking support-standardised branch scores and support-statistic features as input, reduces expected calibration error on the held-out modality by at least 30% relative to support-only LOO-Z fusion, with image AUROC within 1 point.
B1-g1-o4.rationale: Parent 1 (Fisher) calibrates against support normals but has no notion of what abnormal scores look like; parent 2 (Platt) learns a calibrator but from synthetic anomalies whose realism reviewers doubted. A different source of abnormal evidence is already available: the source modalities have real labelled normal and abnormal validation images. Simulating the deployment situation (K supports, unseen test images) on each source modality and learning how fused scores relate to labels transfers calibration knowledge across modalities without synthetic data or target labels — a meta-learning view of fusion.
B1-g1-o4.method: 1) For each source modality m and 200 episodes: sample K normal supports from valid/good of m; score 64 other validation images of m (balanced) with LOO-Z per-branch scores. 2) Features per image: [Z_zero top-2%, Z_few top-2%, Z_zero max, Z_few max, log K, support LOO score std per branch]. 3) Train logistic regression (L2, C = 1) on all episodes of all source modalities (target excluded). 4) Deployment on the target: compute features with its supports; p = sigmoid(w^T x + b). 5) Code: new script train_calibrator.py (uses MVFA checkpoints trained without the target), scoring.py apply_calibrator(). No adapter retraining.
B1-g1-o4.experiment: BMAD leave-one-modality-out (RESC and OCT17 held out together); MVFA checkpoints selected on source-modality validation splits and the MVFA baseline re-run the same way; K in {2,4,8,16}; 3 seeds x 3 support draws, mean and std. Baselines: LOO-Z with logistic mapping fitted on supports only; Fisher p-value fusion; synthetic-Platt calibration. Ablations: feature set; number of episodes; per-modality vs pooled calibrator. Metrics: ECE (15 bins), Brier score, AUROC, sensitivity at p = 0.5. Falsification: ECE reduction below 30% or AUROC loss above 2 points.
provenance: Fed-LoRA: Cross-Domain Generative Knowledge Feedback for Few-Shot Medical Anomaly Detection

B1-g1-o5.title: Image-versus-support two-sample testing: deciding each image by an MMD test against the support normals' patch distribution
B1-g1-o5.summary: Treat each test image's adapted patch tokens as a sample and test whether it comes from the same distribution as the support normals' patches with a kernel MMD statistic and a permutation p-value, giving a per-image, calibrated decision without test-set normalisation.
B1-g1-o5.hypothesis: Per-image MMD permutation p-values against support-normal patches yield image AUROC within 2 points of MVFA's transductive fusion on held-out BMAD modalities with K >= 4, and the realised false-positive rate at p <= 0.05 stays within 5 points of nominal.
B1-g1-o5.rationale: The parent compares single patches to a Gaussian model of normal patches; by analogy with two-sample hypothesis testing, a whole image can be compared to the support set as distributions. The null hypothesis (the test image's patches are drawn like normal support patches) gives a p-value by permutation that is calibrated by construction for exchangeable normal images, which directly answers the problem's request for a label-free, transferable threshold. Anomalies, being localised, shift a fraction of the patch distribution; to keep sensitivity, the statistic is computed on the image's most atypical patches (top 10% by distance to the support bank).
B1-g1-o5.method: 1) Per level l, support set S_l = adapted patch tokens of K support normals (K x 289). 2) For a test image, T_l = its 29 patches (10%) with the highest 1 - max cosine to S_l; reference R_l = 29 random patches of each support image's own top-10% set (computed leave-one-out), pooled. 3) MMD^2 with a Gaussian kernel (median-heuristic bandwidth) between T_l and R_l; statistic = sum over levels. 4) Permutation p-value with 500 permutations (vectorised on GPU). 5) Decision at p <= alpha; score for AUROC = -log p. 6) Code: scoring.py mmd_test(); test_few.py per image; no retraining.
B1-g1-o5.experiment: BMAD leave-one-modality-out (RESC and OCT17 held out together); MVFA checkpoints selected on source-modality validation splits and the MVFA baseline re-run the same way; K in {2,4,8,16}; 3 seeds x 3 support draws, mean and std. Baselines: transductive MVFA; LOO-Z; Mahalanobis scoring. Ablations: top-fraction (5/10/20%); kernel bandwidth; levels used. Metrics: image AUROC, realised FPR at alpha in {0.01, 0.05, 0.1}, sensitivity, runtime per image. Falsification: AUROC loss > 3 points or FPR deviation > 10 points.
provenance: Bridging Vision Foundation Model Priors with CLIP for Spatial-aware Few-shot Anomaly Detection in Medical Images

B1-g1-o6.title: Extreme-value tail calibration of MVFA branch scores from support normals
B1-g1-o6.summary: Fit a generalised Pareto distribution to the upper tail of each branch's support-normal LOO patch scores and convert test scores to tail probabilities, giving per-image scores that remain discriminative beyond the range seen in the supports.
B1-g1-o6.hypothesis: EVT tail probabilities fitted on support-normal LOO scores give per-image fused scores whose image AUROC is within 1 point of MVFA's transductive fusion and whose realised false-positive rate at a nominal 5% tail level is within 5 points of nominal for K >= 4, outperforming clipped z-scores on calibration (ECE) by at least 20%.
B1-g1-o6.rationale: Parent 1 (Platt) learns a mapping but needs anomalies; parent 2 (LOO-Z) needs no anomalies but its Gaussian z-scores are poor descriptions of heavy-tailed anomaly scores, and empirical p-values saturate at 1/(N+1). A different explanation of calibration under normal-only references is extreme-value theory: exceedances of a high threshold by normal patch scores follow a generalised Pareto distribution, which can be fitted from a few hundred support patches and extrapolated to the far tail where anomalies lie.
B1-g1-o6.method: 1) Per branch b and level l, collect support LOO patch scores (K x 289). 2) Choose u_bl = 90th percentile; fit GPD(xi, beta) to exceedances by maximum likelihood (scipy.stats.genpareto), with xi constrained to [-0.5, 0.5] for stability. 3) Tail probability for a test patch score s: P(S > s) = 0.1 * (1 + xi (s - u)/beta)^(-1/xi) for s > u, else the empirical survival. 4) Fuse branches and levels with Fisher's statistic -2 sum log P; image score = top-2% mean; image threshold from support LOO image statistics. 5) Code: scoring.py fit_gpd(), tail_prob(); no retraining.
B1-g1-o6.experiment: BMAD leave-one-modality-out (RESC and OCT17 held out together); MVFA checkpoints selected on source-modality validation splits and the MVFA baseline re-run the same way; K in {2,4,8,16}; 3 seeds x 3 support draws, mean and std. Baselines: LOO-Z; empirical p-value (Fisher) fusion; transductive MVFA. Ablations: tail threshold (85/90/95th percentile); GPD vs exponential tail. Metrics: AUROC, ECE, realised FPR at nominal levels, GPD goodness-of-fit (KS) on support data. Falsification: no ECE gain over LOO-Z or AUROC loss > 2 points.
provenance: Fed-LoRA: Cross-Domain Generative Knowledge Feedback for Few-Shot Medical Anomaly Detection
MadCLIP: Few-shot Medical Anomaly Detection with CLIP
Beyond Static Anchors: Bounded Prototype Conditioning for Language-Free Medical Anomaly Detection

B1-g2-o1.title: Episode-calibrated weighted Fisher fusion: learning per-level weights of support p-values on source-modality episodes
B1-g2-o1.summary: Compute per-level, per-branch empirical p-values against the target's support normals (inductive, distribution-free) and combine them with weights and a logistic mapping learned on simulated K-shot episodes from the source modalities' labelled validation images.
B1-g2-o1.hypothesis: Weighted Fisher fusion with episode-learned level/branch weights improves image AUROC by at least 1 point and reduces expected calibration error by at least 25% relative to unweighted Fisher fusion on held-out BMAD modalities for K >= 4, without any target labels.
B1-g2-o1.rationale: Parent 1 (Fisher) gives every level and branch equal weight although the reviews and MVFA's own ablations suggest levels differ in usefulness; parent 2 (episode calibrator) learns from real source abnormal images but on hand-chosen features. Using the eight -log p terms (4 levels x 2 branches) as the calibrator's features keeps Fisher's distribution-free, support-anchored inputs and lets real labelled source data decide how much each level and branch should count. Because the inputs are p-values relative to each episode's own supports, they are on the same scale across modalities, which addresses the reviewers' concern about cross-modality transfer of the calibrator.
B1-g2-o1.method: 1) Episodes: for each source modality, 200 episodes of K normal supports (valid/good) and 64 balanced validation images. 2) For each image, features x = [mean of top-2% of -log p_bl over pixels] for b in {zero, few}, l in 1..4 (8 features), p from LOO support nulls as in Fisher-MVFA. 3) Logistic regression with non-negative weights (projected gradient), L2 = 1.0, pooled over source episodes. 4) Target: same features with the target supports; probability p = sigma(w^T x + b); threshold at p = 0.5 and at the 95% support-specificity point. 5) Code: train_calibrator.py (episodes), scoring.py fisher_features(); no adapter retraining.
B1-g2-o1.experiment: BMAD leave-one-modality-out (RESC and OCT17 held out together); MVFA checkpoints selected on source-modality validation splits and the MVFA baseline re-run the same way; K in {2,4,8,16}; 3 seeds x 3 support draws, mean and std. Baselines: unweighted Fisher; episode calibrator on raw score features; LOO-Z. Ablations: non-negativity constraint; per-level vs per-branch weights only. Metrics: AUROC, ECE, Brier, sensitivity/specificity at both thresholds; learned weights per held-out fold (interpretability). Falsification: no AUROC or ECE gain over unweighted Fisher.
provenance: Fed-LoRA: Cross-Domain Generative Knowledge Feedback for Few-Shot Medical Anomaly Detection
Fine-Tuning CLIP Models with Convolutional Features for Medical Anomaly Detection

B1-g2-o2.title: Neyman-Pearson likelihood-ratio scoring: a support-normal density against a cross-modality abnormal density learned on source data
B1-g2-o2.summary: Score each test patch by the log-ratio between a density of 'generic abnormal' patch features learned from source modalities' abnormal images and a density of the target's support-normal patches, giving the most powerful per-image test at a chosen false-positive level.
B1-g2-o2.hypothesis: Likelihood-ratio scores combining a target support-normal Gaussian and a source-abnormal Gaussian mixture improve image AUROC by at least 1.5 points over normal-only Fisher fusion on held-out BMAD modalities at K = 2 and K = 4, while the support-derived threshold keeps realised false positives within 5 points of nominal.
B1-g2-o2.rationale: Fisher-MVFA asks only 'how unusual is this patch for a normal image of this modality?', the classical one-class question. By the Neyman-Pearson lemma, the most powerful test at a fixed false-positive rate compares the likelihood under normal and under abnormal hypotheses. MVFA's adapted features are trained to make abnormal patches of all modalities move in a common 'abnormal' direction (alignment to the abnormal text anchor), so an abnormal density estimated on source modalities may transfer, while the normal density must come from the target supports. This turns the scoring problem into a two-sided test without target anomalies.
B1-g2-o2.method: 1) Abnormal model: on source modalities' abnormal images, collect adapted patch tokens from the top-2% patches (images with masks: true lesion patches, used only for source-side density fitting; images without masks: top-2% by zero-shot score), PCA to 64 dims (fitted on source), Gaussian mixture with 8 components. 2) Normal model: Ledoit-Wolf Gaussian on the target supports' patch tokens in the same PCA space. 3) Patch score = log p_abn(f) - log p_nor(f), summed over levels; image score = top-2% mean. 4) Threshold: 95th percentile of support LOO image scores. 5) Code: fit_abnormal_gmm.py, scoring.py lr_score(); no adapter retraining.
B1-g2-o2.experiment: BMAD leave-one-modality-out (RESC and OCT17 held out together); MVFA checkpoints selected on source-modality validation splits and the MVFA baseline re-run the same way; K in {2,4,8,16}; 3 seeds x 3 support draws, mean and std. Baselines: Fisher fusion; Mahalanobis normal-only; transductive MVFA. Ablations: number of components; abnormal model from images without masks only; PCA dimension. Metrics: image/pixel AUROC, realised FPR, sensitivity at the threshold. Falsification: AUROC gain below 0.5 points.
provenance: Bridging Vision Foundation Model Priors with CLIP for Spatial-aware Few-shot Anomaly Detection in Medical Images
AA-CLIP: Enhancing Zero-Shot Anomaly Detection via Anomaly-Aware CLIP

B1-g2-o3.title: Nearest-source-modality calibration transfer: calibrating an unseen modality with the source modalities its supports resemble
B1-g2-o3.summary: Measure how similar the target's support normals are to each source modality in adapted feature space, and transfer the score-to-probability calibration learned on source episodes with weights proportional to that similarity.
B1-g2-o3.hypothesis: Similarity-weighted transfer of source-episode calibrations reduces ECE on the held-out modality by at least 20% relative to a uniformly pooled source calibrator, and the improvement is largest for held-out modalities with a close source neighbour (e.g. LiverCT with BrainMRI as nearest source) and smallest for isolated ones (HIS).
B1-g2-o3.rationale: Both parents rely on a reference to decide what a score means — Fisher on the target's supports (normal side only), the episode calibrator on all source modalities equally (both sides). The reviewers questioned whether calibration learned on very different modalities transfers. A different explanation of transfer is similarity: calibration should transfer from source modalities whose normal feature distribution resembles the target's, which can be measured from the support normals alone. This gives a label-free, interpretable rule for how much each source modality should inform the target's calibration.
B1-g2-o3.method: 1) Per source modality m, fit a calibrator c_m (logistic on Fisher features) from source episodes as in the episode calibrator. 2) Similarity: mean adapted CLS feature of the target supports vs. each source modality's mean normal CLS feature; weights w_m = softmax(-d_m / T), d_m the cosine distance, T selected on source leave-one-source-out episodes. 3) Target probability p = sum_m w_m c_m(x). 4) Code: train_calibrator.py per modality; scoring.py similarity_weights().
B1-g2-o3.experiment: BMAD leave-one-modality-out (RESC and OCT17 held out together); MVFA checkpoints selected on source-modality validation splits and the MVFA baseline re-run the same way; K in {2,4,8,16}; 3 seeds x 3 support draws, mean and std. Baselines: pooled source calibrator; unweighted Fisher with support threshold; nearest-single-modality calibrator. Metrics: ECE, Brier, AUROC, similarity weights per fold, correlation between nearest-source distance and ECE. Falsification: no ECE gain over pooled calibration.
provenance: Fed-LoRA: Cross-Domain Generative Knowledge Feedback for Few-Shot Medical Anomaly Detection
Fine-Tuning CLIP Models with Convolutional Features for Medical Anomaly Detection

B1-g2-o4.title: Risk-controlled abstention band: per-image MVFA decisions that defer when support evidence is insufficient
B1-g2-o4.summary: Turn per-image MVFA scores into three-way decisions (normal, abnormal, defer) using a lower and an upper threshold calibrated on source-modality episodes to control the error rate on non-deferred images, reporting risk-coverage curves instead of a single AUROC.
B1-g2-o4.hypothesis: With thresholds calibrated on source episodes for a 5% error target, the abstention band keeps the error rate on non-deferred target images at or below 7% while deferring at most 30% of images for K >= 4, whereas a single threshold at the same coverage has an error rate above 12% on at least two held-out modalities.
B1-g2-o4.rationale: The parent learns one calibration mapping from source episodes and must commit on every image, which the reviews noted is fragile when the source-to-target transfer of calibration fails. By analogy with selective prediction in safety-critical systems (and with how radiologists escalate uncertain studies), a detector can be made reliable by abstaining in the score region where source episodes show that errors concentrate. The deferral rate itself becomes a measurable, clinically meaningful cost, directly addressing the uncertainty gap in MVFA's evaluation.
B1-g2-o4.method: 1) Per-image score: LOO-Z or Fisher fused score (support-anchored). 2) On source episodes (200 per source modality), choose (t_low, t_high) minimising deferral subject to error on non-deferred images <= 5% (Learn-then-Test style procedure with a binomial bound at confidence 0.9). 3) Target: normal if score < t_low, abnormal if > t_high, defer otherwise. 4) Report risk-coverage curves and the area under them. 5) Code: calibrate_abstention.py; scoring.py decide(); no retraining.
B1-g2-o4.experiment: BMAD leave-one-modality-out (RESC and OCT17 held out together); MVFA checkpoints selected on source-modality validation splits and the MVFA baseline re-run the same way; K in {2,4,8,16}; 3 seeds x 3 support draws, mean and std. Baselines: single support threshold; episode-calibrated single threshold. Metrics: error on non-deferred images, deferral rate, risk-coverage AUC, sensitivity on non-deferred abnormal images. Falsification: error target violated by more than 3 points.
provenance: Fed-LoRA: Cross-Domain Generative Knowledge Feedback for Few-Shot Medical Anomaly Detection

B1-g2-o5.title: Adaptive S-norm for MVFA: cohort score normalisation borrowed from speaker verification
B1-g2-o5.summary: Normalise each test image's anomaly score both against the target supports (Z-norm) and against how the same image scores against memory banks built from a cohort of other modalities' normal images (T-norm), and average the two, as speaker-verification systems do to make one threshold work across speakers.
B1-g2-o5.hypothesis: Adaptive S-norm reduces the spread of the optimal threshold across held-out BMAD modalities by at least 40% and improves balanced accuracy at a single global threshold by at least 3 points over support-only normalisation, with image AUROC within 1 point.
B1-g2-o5.rationale: Speaker verification faced the same problem as per-image MVFA scoring: raw match scores are not comparable across speakers, so one threshold fails. Its solution is cohort normalisation: Z-norm uses the enrolment model's score distribution on impostor data, T-norm uses the test utterance's scores against a cohort of other models, and S-norm averages them, giving thresholds that transfer across speakers. In MVFA, the 'enrolment' is the target support bank and a natural cohort is the normal images of the source modalities: if a test image is unusual even against unrelated normal banks only to the same degree as normal target images are, it is not anomalous.
B1-g2-o5.method: 1) Cohort: for each source modality, a memory bank from 16 normal validation images (adapted tokens per level). 2) For a test image x: raw few-shot image score s(x) against the target support bank; Z-norm: (s - mu_Z)/sigma_Z with statistics of support LOO scores; T-norm: (s - mu_T(x))/sigma_T(x) where mu_T, sigma_T are the mean/std of x's scores against the top-10 most similar cohort banks (adaptive cohort). 3) S-norm = (Z + T)/2, fused with the zero-shot branch's Z-norm score; single global threshold selected on source episodes. 4) Code: build_cohort.py; scoring.py snorm(); no retraining.
B1-g2-o5.experiment: BMAD leave-one-modality-out (RESC and OCT17 held out together); MVFA checkpoints selected on source-modality validation splits and the MVFA baseline re-run the same way; K in {2,4,8,16}; 3 seeds x 3 support draws, mean and std. Baselines: LOO-Z (Z-norm only); Fisher fusion; transductive MVFA. Metrics: AUROC, balanced accuracy and FPR at one global threshold across all held-out modalities, spread of per-modality optimal thresholds. Falsification: no reduction in threshold spread.
provenance: Fed-LoRA: Cross-Domain Generative Knowledge Feedback for Few-Shot Medical Anomaly Detection
Fine-Tuning CLIP Models with Convolutional Features for Medical Anomaly Detection

B1-g2-o6.title: Harmonic-mean p-value fusion with region-mass scoring: per-image MVFA scores that stay valid under dependent levels
B1-g2-o6.summary: Replace Fisher's combination, which assumes independent evidence, with the harmonic mean p-value across MVFA's strongly correlated levels and branches, keeping region-mass pooling and support-derived thresholds.
B1-g2-o6.hypothesis: Harmonic-mean p-value fusion gives realised false-positive rates at the support threshold within 3 points of nominal, versus more than 8 points of excess false positives for Fisher fusion, on held-out BMAD modalities with K >= 4, with image AUROC within 0.5 points of Fisher fusion.
B1-g2-o6.rationale: The four MVFA levels are sequential stages of one ViT and the two branches share the backbone, so their per-patch p-values are strongly positively dependent; Fisher's statistic assumes independence and is anti-conservative under positive dependence, which inflates false positives exactly where calibration is the goal. The harmonic mean p-value is a combination rule that remains approximately valid under arbitrary dependence, so substituting it keeps the parent's framing (support-anchored per-pixel evidence, region pooling, support thresholds) while fixing a statistical flaw the parent inherits.
B1-g2-o6.method: 1) Per-pixel empirical p-values p_bl as in Fisher-MVFA (support LOO nulls). 2) HMP per pixel: H = 8 / sum_{b,l} (1/p_bl); statistic X = -log H. 3) Region-mass pooling on X with t_pix = 99th percentile of support LOO X; image score as before. 4) Report the empirical correlation matrix of the 8 per-pixel p-values on support normals to document dependence. 5) Code: scoring.py hmp_map(); reuse region_mass().
B1-g2-o6.experiment: BMAD leave-one-modality-out (RESC and OCT17 held out together); MVFA checkpoints selected on source-modality validation splits and the MVFA baseline re-run the same way; K in {2,4,8,16}; 3 seeds x 3 support draws, mean and std. Baselines: Fisher + region mass (parent); Bonferroni-style min-p; LOO-Z + region mass. Metrics: realised FPR at nominal 5% and 1%, sensitivity, image/pixel AUROC, PRO, p-value correlation across levels. Falsification: no FPR improvement over Fisher fusion.
provenance: MadCLIP: Few-shot Medical Anomaly Detection with CLIP
Beyond Static Anchors: Bounded Prototype Conditioning for Language-Free Medical Anomaly Detection
AA-CLIP: Enhancing Zero-Shot Anomaly Detection via Anomaly-Aware CLIP

B1-g3-o1.title: FDR-controlled anomaly maps: Benjamini-Yekutieli discoveries per image from support-anchored pixel p-values
B1-g3-o1.summary: Treat every patch of a test image as a hypothesis test against the support normals, apply the Benjamini-Yekutieli procedure (valid under dependence) at a target false discovery rate, and score the image by the mass of discovered patches.
B1-g3-o1.hypothesis: At q = 0.1, the proportion of discovered patches that fall outside true lesions on held-out BrainMRI, LiverCT and RESC images stays at or below 0.15, and the image score 'discovered mass' achieves image AUROC within 1 point of harmonic-mean fusion with region pooling.
B1-g3-o1.rationale: The parent controls error at the image level, but its pixel threshold for regions (99th percentile of support maps) has no statistical meaning. By analogy with voxel-wise inference in neuroimaging, a per-image anomaly map is a multiple-testing problem: hundreds of correlated patch tests, of which a few may be true anomalies. FDR control gives the map itself a guarantee (expected fraction of false patches among flagged ones), which is the clinically relevant quantity for localisation, and the Benjamini-Yekutieli variant holds under arbitrary dependence between neighbouring patches.
B1-g3-o1.method: 1) Per patch, combined p-value across levels and branches with the harmonic mean (support LOO nulls). 2) Per image, Benjamini-Yekutieli at q in {0.05, 0.1, 0.2} over the 289 patches. 3) Image score = number of discoveries (or summed -log p over discoveries); image threshold from support LOO images. 4) Pixel map for evaluation = discoveries upsampled, plus the continuous -log p map for AUROC. 5) Code: scoring.py by_fdr().
B1-g3-o1.experiment: BMAD leave-one-modality-out (RESC and OCT17 held out together); MVFA checkpoints selected on source-modality validation splits and the MVFA baseline re-run the same way; K in {2,4,8,16}; 3 seeds x 3 support draws, mean and std. Baselines: harmonic-mean + region mass; Fisher + top-2%; transductive MVFA. Metrics: realised false discovery proportion of flagged patches (masked datasets), sensitivity per lesion, image AUROC, pixel AUROC, PRO. Falsification: realised FDP above 2q on average.

Beyond Static Anchors: Bounded Prototype Conditioning for Language-Free Medical Anomaly Detection

B1-g3-o2.title: Support-bootstrap uncertainty: deciding on the lower confidence bound of a per-image MVFA score
B1-g3-o2.summary: Resample the K support normals with replacement to obtain a distribution of each test image's support-normalised score, and flag an image only when the lower confidence bound exceeds the threshold, giving per-image uncertainty that grows as K shrinks.
B1-g3-o2.hypothesis: Using the 10th-percentile bootstrap bound reduces false positives at K = 2 and K = 4 by at least 30% relative to the point estimate at the same threshold, with sensitivity loss below 10 points, and the bootstrap interval width correlates with per-image error (Spearman rho >= 0.3).
B1-g3-o2.rationale: By analogy with ensemble forecasting, where the spread of an ensemble indicates the reliability of a prediction, the dependence of a per-image score on which few supports were drawn is itself the main source of uncertainty in MVFA's few-shot mode (one fixed draw in the released code). Bootstrapping the supports quantifies it per image at no labelling cost, and deciding on a lower bound turns that uncertainty into fewer false alarms where evidence is thin.
B1-g3-o2.method: 1) B = 30 bootstrap resamples of the K supports; for each, recompute support statistics (LOO-Z) and the region-mass image score of the test image. 2) Point score = median; lower bound = 10th percentile. 3) Threshold from support LOO scores as before. 4) Cost: memory banks are reused, only statistics recomputed; few-shot distances computed once per support image and indexed. 5) Code: scoring.py bootstrap_scores().
B1-g3-o2.experiment: BMAD leave-one-modality-out (RESC and OCT17 held out together); MVFA checkpoints selected on source-modality validation splits and the MVFA baseline re-run the same way; K in {2,4,8,16}; 3 seeds x 3 support draws, mean and std. Baselines: LOO-Z + region mass point estimate; harmonic-mean fusion. Metrics: FP and sensitivity at the threshold, interval width vs error correlation, image AUROC of median score. Falsification: no FP reduction at K <= 4.
provenance: MadCLIP: Few-shot Medical Anomaly Detection with CLIP
Beyond Static Anchors: Bounded Prototype Conditioning for Language-Free Medical Anomaly Detection

B1-g3-o3.title: E-value fusion: dependence-robust, betting-based per-image anomaly evidence from support normals
B1-g3-o3.summary: Convert each level/branch patch score into an e-value (a likelihood-ratio-like betting score calibrated on the support normals), average e-values across levels and branches — valid under any dependence — and decide by the e-value's guarantee P(E >= 1/alpha) <= alpha.
B1-g3-o3.hypothesis: E-value fusion yields realised false-positive rates at or below nominal (5%) on held-out BMAD modalities for K >= 4 while losing at most 1.5 image AUROC points relative to harmonic-mean p-value fusion.
B1-g3-o3.rationale: Harmonic-mean p-values remain only approximately valid and can be anti-conservative at very small levels. A different, exact route borrowed from game-theoretic statistics is to use e-values: the arithmetic mean of e-values is again an e-value under arbitrary dependence, so MVFA's correlated levels and branches can be combined exactly, and Markov's inequality gives a guaranteed false-positive bound. Calibrating p-values from the support normals into e-values (via a calibrator such as kappa p^(kappa - 1)) needs no labels.
B1-g3-o3.method: 1) Per patch, branch and level, empirical p from support LOO nulls. 2) E-value calibrator e = kappa p^(kappa - 1) with kappa = 0.5 (ablation 0.25, 0.75). 3) Per-patch fused e-value = mean over the 8 terms; image e-value = mean of top-2% patch e-values (an average of e-values remains an e-value under the null); decision at E >= 1/alpha. 4) Code: scoring.py evalue_fusion().
B1-g3-o3.experiment: BMAD leave-one-modality-out (RESC and OCT17 held out together); MVFA checkpoints selected on source-modality validation splits and the MVFA baseline re-run the same way; K in {2,4,8,16}; 3 seeds x 3 support draws, mean and std. B1-g3-o4.title: Test-time-augmentation consensus: scoring an image by anomaly evidence that survives across augmented views
B1-g3-o4.summary: Score several label-preserving augmentations of each test image with per-image p-value fusion and take the minimum (or a low quantile) of the region scores across views, so isolated spurious peaks that do not persist across views no longer decide the image label.
B1-g3-o4.hypothesis: TTA-consensus scoring with 8 views reduces false positives at the support-derived threshold by at least 20% relative to single-view Fisher fusion on held-out BMAD modalities, with image AUROC within 0.5 points and no loss of sensitivity on lesions larger than 1% of the image.
B1-g3-o4.rationale: By analogy with consensus in ensemble and repeated-measurement settings, real lesions produce evidence that is stable under small geometric and intensity perturbations, while single-pixel artefacts of patchification (the verified max-pixel rule's main failure) move or vanish. Requiring consensus across views is a per-image, label-free robustness mechanism complementary to statistical fusion.
B1-g3-o4.method: 1) Views: identity, horizontal flip, rotations +/-5 deg, scale 0.95/1.05, brightness +/-5% (8 views). 2) Per view, Fisher p-value map against support nulls (supports scored with the same views for their LOO nulls), mapped back to the original frame. 3) Pixel consensus map = 25th percentile across views; image score = region mass on the consensus map. 4) Cost: 8 forward passes per image (inference only). 5) Code: scoring.py tta_consensus().
B1-g3-o4.experiment: BMAD leave-one-modality-out (RESC and OCT17 held out together); MVFA checkpoints selected on source-modality validation splits and the MVFA baseline re-run the same way; K in {2,4,8,16}; 3 seeds x 3 support draws, mean and std. Baselines: single-view Fisher with top-2% and with region mass. Ablations: number and type of views; consensus quantile. Metrics: FP per image, sensitivity by lesion size, image/pixel AUROC, runtime. Falsification: FP reduction below 10%.

B1-g3-o5.title: Brown-corrected Fisher fusion: dependence-adjusted p-value combination estimated from support normals, with region-mass pooling
B1-g3-o5.summary: Keep Fisher's powerful combination of per-level, per-branch support p-values but correct its null distribution for the dependence between MVFA's levels and branches using Brown's method with covariances estimated on the support normals, then pool by region mass.
B1-g3-o5.hypothesis: Brown-corrected Fisher fusion keeps realised false-positive rates within 3 points of nominal (like harmonic-mean fusion) while retaining Fisher's image AUROC within 0.3 points, giving at least 0.5 AUROC points more than harmonic-mean fusion on held-out BMAD modalities with K >= 4.
B1-g3-o5.rationale: The two parents trade power for validity: Fisher is powerful but anti-conservative for correlated evidence, the harmonic mean p-value is valid under dependence but can lose power. Brown's method keeps Fisher's statistic and rescales its chi-square null using the covariance of the -2 log p terms, which can be estimated from the support normals' leave-one-out p-values — no labels needed. This combines the strength of each parent and the shared region-mass pooling.
B1-g3-o5.method: 1) Per-pixel empirical p-values p_bl (8 terms) from support LOO nulls. 2) Estimate the covariance of -2 log p_bl across pixels of support normals (LOO), giving Brown's scale c and degrees of freedom f: c = Var(X)/(2E[X]), f = 2E[X]^2/Var(X), with E[X] = 16 under independence. 3) Pixel statistic: Brown p-value = 1 - F_chi2(X/c; f); use -log of it as the pixel map. 4) Region-mass pooling and support-derived thresholds as in the parents. 5) Code: scoring.py brown_fisher(); test_few.py per image.
B1-g3-o5.experiment: BMAD leave-one-modality-out (RESC and OCT17 held out together); MVFA checkpoints selected on source-modality validation splits and the MVFA baseline re-run the same way; K in {2,4,8,16}; 3 seeds x 3 support draws, mean and std. Baselines: Fisher + region mass; harmonic-mean + region mass; LOO-Z + region mass. Metrics: realised FPR at 1% and 5%, sensitivity, image/pixel AUROC, PRO, estimated c and f per modality. Falsification: FPR not within 3 points or AUROC below harmonic-mean fusion.

B1-g3-o6.title: Instance-whitened patch features: per-image scoring that is robust to acquisition shift between supports and test images
B1-g3-o6.summary: Remove per-image style statistics (channel means and variances of adapted patch tokens) before both few-shot matching and support-anchored p-values, so that differences in scanner, contrast or staining between the K supports and a test image do not masquerade as anomalies.
B1-g3-o6.hypothesis: Instance whitening of adapted patch tokens before scoring improves image AUROC by at least 1 point and reduces false positives at the support threshold by at least 15% on held-out modalities when supports and test images are drawn from different acquisition subgroups (simulated by intensity and contrast shifts of the test set), while changing results by less than 0.5 points without shift.
B1-g3-o6.rationale: Support-anchored p-values assume supports and test normals are exchangeable; in practice a site's few supports may come from a different scanner or protocol than later test images (G14). By analogy with instance normalisation in domain generalisation and style transfer, per-image feature statistics carry style rather than content; removing them before comparison makes the support reference transfer across acquisition differences, which the original test-set min-max normalisation partly (and transductively) absorbed.
B1-g3-o6.method: 1) For each image and level, adapted patch tokens F (289 x d): F' = (F - mean_patches(F)) / std_patches(F) per channel, then L2-normalise. 2) Use F' for the few-shot memory bank and test matching; zero-shot branch unchanged. 3) Support nulls and Fisher fusion as before. 4) Shift simulation: apply gamma (0.7-1.3) and contrast changes to test images only. 5) Code: scoring.py instance_whiten(); test_few.py.
B1-g3-o6.experiment: BMAD leave-one-modality-out (RESC and OCT17 held out together); MVFA checkpoints selected on source-modality validation splits and the MVFA baseline re-run the same way; K in {2,4,8,16}; 3 seeds x 3 support draws, mean and std. Baselines: Fisher fusion without whitening; transductive MVFA. Conditions: no shift, simulated shift. Metrics: image/pixel AUROC, FP at threshold, sensitivity. Falsification: no gain under shift or loss above 0.5 points without shift.
